name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals and a motor of less than 750 watts
Class 1 and class 3 assist only while the rider is pedaling, stopping at 20 and 28 mph; class 2 can propel it without pedaling, up to 20 mph
On class 1 and class 3 the motor stops when the rider stops pedaling; on class 2 it stops when the rider brakes or releases or activates a switch
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its top assisted speed unless the label is changed to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Riders under 16 may not operate a class 3, but may ride as a passenger on one designed to carry passengers
Class 3 riders and passengers must wear a helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards
Class 1 and class 2 may be ridden on bicycle and shared-use paths unless the local authority or state agency in charge bans them
Class 3 is kept off bicycle and shared-use paths unless the path is within or next to a highway or the local authority or state agency in charge allows it
No class may be ridden on a mountain biking, hiking, equestrian or other natural-surface trail reserved for nonmotorized use unless the entity in charge allows it
The traffic laws for bicycles apply to it, and violations put no points on the rider's driver's license
Not a motor vehicle or moped: no registration or driver's license
